papers.title: RPFace: From biased structural benchmarks to generalizable RNA-protein interface prediction
papers.abstract: Modeling protein-RNA complexes with co-folding and docking methods is routine, yet these methods are evaluated on benchmarks whose composition mirrors the deposited structures on which they were trained or tuned, leaving open whether their reported performance reflects true generalization. Here, we focus the evaluation on the region that carries the biological signal: the binding interface. For the first time, we construct and release a fair benchmark that stratifies protein-RNA data into distinct structural and experimental groups, providing a more stringent test of generalization than aggregate averages. On this benchmark, we find that accuracy of detecting the binding site using co-folding methods is concentrated in ribosomal complexes and varies systematically with factors such as experimental modality. For docking methods, it is reliable only when the input conformations are already close to the bound state, and it is inconsistent across RNA classes. Both families of methods fail to transfer to in vivo CLIP experiments. To address this gap, we introduce RPFace, to the best of our knowledge the first model that jointly predicts the binding preference of every protein residue and every RNA nucleotide directly from sequence, requiring no experimental structure, template, or multiple sequence alignment. RPFace combines an ensemble of predicted secondary structures with a multi-modal embedding-enrichment scheme that fuses representations from RNA foundation models and structure prediction models. Unlike existing approaches, it is a very small and fast model that delivers stable performance across structural and experimental conditions, is robust to conformational change, and generalizes to in vivo datasets without extensive pretraining. As a result, RPFace matches the state-of-the-art methods on protein interfaces with no evolutionary information, and outperforms them on RNA interfaces, with the largest gains in zero-shot settings despite using only sequence information. The model, code, and data are available at Github.
papers.shortSummary: 기존 co-folding·도킹 성능은 구조군과 실험 조건에 따라 편향되고 CLIP 실험으로 전이되지 않는 반면, RPFace는 서열만으로 단백질 잔기와 RNA 뉴클레오타이드의 결합 선호도를 예측해 더 일관된 일반화를 보인다는 주장이다.
papers.whyCare: 구조 기반 복합체 예측이 잘 맞는 구조군에 편중될 수 있고, 그 성능이 in vivo 결합으로 이어지지 않는다는 문제를 명시적으로 시험한다. RPFace의 주장이 재현되면 구조가 없는 RNA-결합 후보를 서열에서 선별하는 별도 분석 경로가 생길 수 있다.
papers.skepticism: 초록에는 분할별 표본 수, 유사 서열·구조 누출 통제, 평가 지표, CLIP 라벨 처리, 불확실성 및 기준선별 정량 결과가 제시되지 않아 일반화 주장의 크기를 판단하기 어렵다. 특히 구조 복합체의 홀드아웃 성능과 CLIP 신호 예측은 서로 다른 평가 문제이므로 별도로 확인해야 한다.

papers.title: Deploying liquid intelligence in cancer: Finding answers in our blood
papers.abstract: Liquid biopsies are one of the few noninvasive procedures for probing disease at the molecular level. They represent a scalable solution to cancer detection and monitoring by capturing tumor-derived signals from circulating biomolecules such as proteins, DNA, RNA, and metabolites. However, these signals are often sparse, heterogeneous, and shaped by genetics, demographics, and comorbidities. Recent advances in artificial intelligence, especially with multimodal foundation models, have proven capable of extracting signals from noisy, high-dimensional data. Pretraining on large cohorts and integrating complementary modalities may improve sensitivity for tumor signals in blood, though significant clinical and infrastructural barriers remain. This review synthesizes advances in liquid biopsy technologies and artificial intelligence and examines how their convergence can enable enhanced cancer monitoring.
papers.shortSummary: 혈액의 단백질·DNA·RNA·대사체 신호를 이용한 liquid biopsy와 AI의 접점을 정리한 리뷰다. 희소하고 개인차가 큰 신호를 multimodal foundation model과 대규모 사전학습으로 통합하는 전략을 다룬다. 새 편집기나 단일 실험 기술을 제시한 연구가 아니라 암 모니터링 분야의 기술·인프라 방향을 정리한 글이다.

papers.takeaway: 여러 생체 신호의 일치성을 이용해 약한 질환 신호를 해석하려는 방향이다.
papers.skepticism: 서로 다른 modality를 더하는 이득을 어떤 benchmark와 일반화 기준으로 평가하는가?
papers.blurb: 혈액의 단백질·DNA·RNA·대사체 신호를 이용한 liquid biopsy와 AI의 접점을 정리한 리뷰다.

papers.title: Harmonized brain ontology and 3D atlases for human, macaque, and marmoset basal ganglia
papers.abstract: A major goal of the BRAIN Initiative Cell Atlas Network (BICAN) is to create a suite of foundational reference cell atlases and associated standards for human and nonhuman primate brains. Central to this goal is the creation of cross-species-harmonized cellular taxonomies and structural parcellations with formal ontologies that can be mapped onto 3D reference frameworks, bridging neuroimaging and cellular and histological resolutions. We describe an iterative approach, focused initially on the basal ganglia, to co-create structural and cellular ontologies for human, macaque, and marmoset brains and to map and refine structural parcellations into neuroimaging-based common coordinate frameworks. We create a Harmonized Ontology of Mammalian Brain Anatomy (HOMBA) to meet these needs. These references provide the framework for documenting and mapping all experimental sampling in BICAN, allowing analyses of cellular and molecular variation as a function of topographic position and enabling comparisons of cellular, molecular, and neuroimaging-based functional variation across species.
papers.shortSummary: BICAN의 human·macaque·marmoset 자료를 연결할 구조·세포 ontology와 3D reference framework를 구성했다. basal ganglia부터 해부학적 구획과 세포 taxonomy를 공동으로 맞추고 neuroimaging 좌표에 연결했다. HOMBA를 제시해 세포·분자·영상 자료를 종과 위치 사이에서 비교할 기반을 제공했다.

papers.takeaway: 다른 종의 atlas를 연결하려면 이름 대응과 공간 대응을 함께 표준화해야 한다.
